FOREWORD

This Indian Standard which is identical with IEC Pub 870-I-3 ( 1990 ) `Telecontrol equipment and systems - Part 1 : General considerations, Section 3 Glossary', issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission ( IEC ), was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendations of the Power Line Carrier Systems and Associated Telecontrol Equipment Sectional Committee ( LTD 25 > and approval of the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. INTRODUCTION
Standards during the and reports last few years on telecontrol eqtipment and systems produced by IEC Technical Committee No. 57 in different

documents use a certain number of terms with specific meanings in telecontrol applications that are not yet defined in IEC Publication 50(371) : International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (IEV), Chapter 371: Telecontrol (1984),

This report nitions and Chapter 371.

presents includes

- in alphabetic those terms

order - these terms and their defithat are already defined in IEV

This report presents a comprehensive particular mei-tning in telecontrol systems tised in future telecontrol documentation.

means of referring and equipment that

to terms with should also be

With respect to the current work on telecontrol documentation and the necessity of defining the new important terms, it should be emphasized that this report will be followed by addenda in due course.

1.

Scope This series of standards applies tc, telecontrol equipment and systems with coded bit serial data transmission for monitoring and control of geographically widespread processes.

2.

Object This report covers those. terms which are specifically relevant telecontrol technique`s as well as other terms which are necessary the understanding of telecontrol standards. This report also gives, dictionaries of electrical and where applicable, electronic terms. references to to for

other

Terms which are considered to be well known by readers of tele-. control standards are not included in this report. This applies particularly in the field of communications where such terms as, for "information" and "bit" are commonplace and well understood. example,

IS 12746 ( Part l/Set 3) : 1993 IEC Pub 670-1-3 (1990) Instruction command: standard command

A command which is input at a control centre and which indicates a standard instruction to operators in the control room `of a manned station (IEV 371-03-17). Examples: "Start generators" or "Adjust generator output to
. . . MW"

NOTE - The instruction command is distinguished from instructions transmitted by general communication means (e.g. teleprinter) in that it is input and transmitted by means of devices tised in telecontrol systems for other purposes and therefore must be programmed in a similar manner to other types of commands.

centre control (ACC)

Load-frequency

generation

The regulation of the power output of electric generators within a prescribed area in response to changes in system frequency, tie line loading or the relation of these to each other so as to maintain the scheduled system frequency or established interchange with other areas within pre-determined limits or both (1).

Load

shedding

The process of deliberately removing preselected loads from a power system in response to an abnormal condition in order to maintain the stability of the system (1).

Local/Remote

switch system of a station which allows the choice of

A part of the control local or remote operation.

Maintainability Maintainability is the ability of a system or equipment, under gfven conditions of use, to be restored to full working order after detection of fault and to be maintained. during normal working operation.

Maintained

command

A command in which the output signal to operational equipment is maintained until the change of state is executed or until the end of a predetermined delay longer than the response of the slowest operational equipment; the duration of the output signal is independent of the duration of the initiating signal (IEV 371-03-05).

Overall

accuracy

The deviation between the destination and the source values of information which undergoes a conversion from digital to analog form, or vice versa, expressed in per cent of the nominal full range value.

18

IS 12746 (Part l/Set 3) : 1993
IEC Pub 670-l-3 (1990)

Overall

information

transmissioti

efficiency content for the of a trans-

The ratio of the correctly transferred information of the time required message in bits to the product mission of that message and the bit transmission rate.

NOTE - The calculation of the overall transmission efficiency shall consider delays caused by transmission of polling frames, acknowledgement frames; average delays expended for error recovery, round trip propagation delays of signels, etc.

Overall

Telecontrol

system

A telecontrol system serves for monitoring and control of processes which are geographically widespread. This includes all equipment and functions for acquisition, processing, transmission and display of the necessary process information.

transfer

time signal from the peripheral the sending station, to the to its peripheral equipment equipoutput at the

NOTE The telecontrol transfer time includes time delay for signal conversion, coding, etc., in the telecontrol transmitter, signal delay decoding, on the transmission channel and time delay for reconversion, etc., checking, in the telecontrol receiver. Stnadard Mark

Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
